title: Understanding the Project Structure
description: What do all these folders and files do?

slides.title: Key Files and Folders 📁
slides.content:
# Let’s Break It Down

* **`pom.xml`** – Maven’s configuration file. It lists dependencies, plugins, and build settings.
* **`src/main/java`** – Your Java source code goes here.
* **`src/main/resources`** – Configuration files, templates, and static assets.
* **`application.properties`** – Where you set properties like server port, database URLs, etc.
* **`src/test`** – Unit and integration tests.

You’ll spend most of your time in `src/main/java` and `src/main/resources`.

slides.title: The Main Class
slides.content: Spring Boot needs a **main** class to bootstrap the application. It looks like this:

quizData.question: What is the purpose of the `@SpringBootApplication` annotation?

options.text: It marks a class as a REST controller
It tells Spring Boot to run a SQL script
It enables auto‑configuration and component scanning
It is required for every Java class

quizData.explanation: `@SpringBootApplication` is a convenience annotation that includes `@Configuration`, `@EnableAutoConfiguration`, and `@ComponentScan`. It tells Spring Boot to set up the application with sensible defaults.
